clue.text: Consume a small bird

definitions.meaning: to eat or drink something down, taking it in
a fork-tailed songbird that migrates in summer

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to eat up a little bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To gulp food down is one sense, and the same word names a migrating fork-tailed bird.

clue.text: Rushed off, and so 'made an impression on a top newsman

parts.note: to stamp is to press a mark onto something
ED is short for editor, the top journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: Someone stormed off after making their mark on the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd or crowd charging away in panic.

clue.text: Excuse sailors love making

parts.note: an AB is an able seaman, so sailors are ABS

indicators.note: making suggests building something new from the word love

explanation.surface: Sailors make love as an excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges LOVE into OLVE after ABS.
explanation.definitionFit: To pardon or free from blame.

clue.text: He must watch his language!

parts.note: the idiom about not swearing is read literally: one who follows speech by looking at the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: A deaf person understanding speech by watching lip movements literally watches words.

clue.text: This might shed some 'light on things North of the Border

definitions.text: This might shed some 'light on things North of the Border

parts.words: This might shed some 'light on things North of the Border
parts.note: a candle's thread gives light; also a town in the far north of Scotland, north of the English border

explanation.definitionFit: The burning cord of a candle, and a Highland Scottish town.

clue.text: The entertainer's attire's fantastic!

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wild and fanciful, so these letters are wildly rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word attire's, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A performer's costume is praised as marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The entertainer's' is the definition with its 's standing for 'is', the link to the rest; 'fantastic' shuffles ATTIRES.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer, especially a singer or dancer in variety, is called by this French-derived word.

clue.text: 23 man is made to: run

indicators.note: made in the sense of made over, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: 23 refers to the answer to 23 down, TIRED

explanation.surface: A tired man is forced to run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges TIRED and MAN IS; 'to' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage or direct an organisation.

clue.text: 'A little, extra, it, appears, and that's characteristic

indicators.note: a little of the phrase means only a part of it is taken

explanation.surface: A small extra thing appears and that's typical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little' takes part of EXTRA IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguishing feature or quality.

clue.text: "Respectable Professors of the Dismal -", wrote Carlyle

definitions.text: "Respectable Professors of the Dismal -", wrote Carlyle

parts.words: "Respectable Professors of the Dismal -", wrote Carlyle
parts.note: Thomas Carlyle called economics the dismal discipline; the missing word completes his phrase

explanation.definitionFit: Carlyle's name for economics was 'the dismal' study, using the word for systematic knowledge.

clue.text: A high-flier on the course?

parts.note: a bird of prey flies high; on a golf course the same word is two under par

explanation.definitionFit: A large raptor, and a golf score of two strokes under par.

clue.text: A regressive attitude for a writer

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the word for an attitude is read from the end

parts.note: an attitude or posture struck is a pose

explanation.surface: A backward-looking outlook suits a certain author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressive' turns POSE round to ESOP, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek teller of fables is a classic example of an author.

clue.text: Putting up some resistance to an approach about a club

indicators.note: about means going round, so the approach word surrounds the club

parts.note: an approach or arrival is a coming
a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: Someone resists the advance of a person waving a cudgel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts BAT inside COMING, after its COM.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting against something is offering it opposition.

clue.text: Invested everything in very dear bed

indicators.note: invested means placed or put in, so one word is set inside another
in marks where everything goes: within the word for very dear

parts.note: someone very dear is a pet, a darling
everything is all

explanation.surface: Someone sank all their money into a very expensive bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invested ... in' puts ALL inside PET; 'very dear' looks like a price but means a darling.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw mattress or makeshift sleeping place on the floor.

clue.text: An insect mutation for example

indicators.note: a mutation is a change of form, so the letters change their order

explanation.surface: A mutated bug serves as a case in point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutation' rearranges AN INSECT; 'for' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A single case cited to illustrate a point is a synonym.

clue.text: The cake-shop in question is, past the lake

indicators.note: in question means doubtful, so the letters of is past are unsettled

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Someone says the bakery is beyond the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in question' rearranges IS PAST into PATISS, then ERIE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A French pastry shop.

clue.text: Anxiety makes the dunderhead study

parts.note: read as the head of 'dunder', its first letter
to study a subject at university is to read it

explanation.surface: A fool is made nervous by having to study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' looks like a fool but is split as 'dunder' plus its head, giving D; READ for 'study' is a British university usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Great fear or apprehension is a synonym for anxiety.

clue.text: Dope gets in, they agree

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
to get in is to enter, so gets in is enters

explanation.surface: A drug gets smuggled in and the officials nod it through.
explanation.definitionFit: People who consent or concur are those who agree.

clue.text: Experienced sailor managed set-up and no-one capsized, so the story goes

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means put upwards, so the sailor and managed words are read backwards

parts.note: an old tar is an experienced sailor
to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: capsized means turned upside down, so no-one is read backwards

parts.note: no plus one, the one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An old sailor organised things and nobody overturned, as the tale is told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' turns TARRAN into NARRAT; 'capsized' turns NOI into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling of events, the way a tale is recounted.

clue.text: A 19 dividing animal enclosure as legally required

indicators.note: dividing means splitting the enclosure word with the others

parts.note: a sty is a pig pen
19 is TRAINER; a tutor is a trainer

explanation.surface: A coach separates an animal pen as the law demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dividing' puts A TUTOR inside STY; TUTOR is a synonym for the answer to 19.
explanation.definitionFit: Required by statute, laid down by law.

clue.text: To advise against a destructive device needed resolve

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or advise against
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: Determination was needed to warn people off a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide firmly or settle on something is to resolve it.

clue.text: Suite taken ahead of Her Majesty in a coach

indicators.note: taken ahead of means the suite word comes first

parts.note: a train is a retinue or suite of attendants
ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The royal entourage goes ahead of the Queen in a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like the carriage of the surface but means a sports trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who instructs athletes is a coach.

clue.text: Girl soldiers without a carrier

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the soldiers go round the carrier

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A girl's troops find themselves without transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: RA goes round HOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: A cover-up in the main

definitions.meaning: a protective garment worn over clothes

explanation.surface: A garment worn over clothes and the phrase meaning generally.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose protective garment, and generally speaking.

clue.text: Correct, though the hunt may hold it's incorrect

indicators.note: may hold means could contain, so the hunt word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a hunt is a chase

indicators.note: incorrect means wrong, so the letters of it's are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A remark admits the hunt could be holding something wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrect' gives TIS from IT'S, which 'may hold' puts inside CHASE, after its CHAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To punish or reprimand someone is to correct them.

clue.text: Doubly firm over a drink

indicators.note: doubly means the firm abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company firm goes over to a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link: CO twice then A.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate beverage.

clue.text: Turning up a German article it is so hackneyed!

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means reading the words from the bottom upwards

parts.note: der is the German definite article

explanation.surface: A German item proves to be very stale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' reverses DERIT; 'is so' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn out from overuse, stale.

clue.text: Entrance, to a university. is a piece of cake, to say the least

definitions.text: piece of cake, to say the least

parts.note: an entrance is a gate

explanation.surface: Getting into university is said to be easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of cake' suggests something easy; 'to say the least' hints that the answer is a whole rich cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich cream cake is more than merely a slice of sponge.

clue.text: Just a little lower

parts.note: lower read as one that lows, a cow; a little one is a young bovine

explanation.definitionFit: A young cow, and the muscular back of the leg.

clue.text: Many in time look back — such .-a bloomer!

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: back means the word for a look is turned round

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: Many people look back over time at such an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look back' turns AIR into RIA; 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-like garden plant grown for its flowers is a flowerer.

clue.text: State it's the same with a small house

parts.note: id. is short for idem, Latin for the same
HO is an abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Someone says it's the same story with a little home.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the north-west.

clue.text: Cut, but only for a span

parts.note: a bridge spans a gap

explanation.surface: A cut that only lasts for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'span' suggests a period of time but is a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text is to cut it down.

clue.text: Friend is after a bit of fish at the last moment

indicators.note: is after means the friend comes behind the bit of fish

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend is chasing some fish at the eleventh hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of fish' suggests a morsel to eat, but is a fin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lastly, after a long delay, at the end.
